title: Knowledge, Awareness, and Risk Perception of West Nile Virus (WNV) Among the General Population and Healthcare Professionals
summary:
West Nile virus (WNV) is a mosquito-borne arbovirus that has become increasingly established in Europe in recent years and is now also causing autochthonous (locally acquired) infections in Germany. As part of this study, adults in Frankfurt am Main and individuals affiliated with the healthcare system in Germany will be surveyed regarding their knowledge, risk perception, and information needs concerning West Nile virus.
Effective prevention depends largely on an adequate level of knowledge among both the general population and healthcare professionals, a realistic perception of risk, and health communication tailored to the needs of specific target groups.

interventions.name: One-time online survey of the adult general population in Frankfurt am Main, as well as adults affiliated with the healthcare system in Germany, assessing their knowledge, risk perception, and information needs regarding West Nile virus.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
The inclusion criteria are an age of at least 18 years; residence, place of work, vocational training, or study location in Frankfurt am Main (general population) or anywhere in Germany (healthcare professionals); sufficient German language proficiency to understand the study information and questionnaire; and voluntary informed consent to participate in the study.
Exclusion criteria:
The exclusion criteria are an age below 18 years, lack of informed consent, and incomplete datasets that are not sufficiently complete to be included in the analysis.
Minors and individuals lacking the capacity to provide informed consent will not be included in the study.
